userStories.title: P2.1 harness — fix the hung realtime-gateway.integration-spec.ts teardown so both realtime integration specs exit cleanly
userStories.description: As an executor or orchestrator running the realtime integration slice, I want realtime-gateway.integration-spec.ts to tear down every socket and Redis handle it opens so that the run finishes green and the jest process exits instead of hanging forever, unblocking the standing orchestrator item and every later realtime integration story.
acceptanceCriteria: PLAN anchor (phase-02-report, verbatim): "NODE_ENV=test npx jest --config jest-integration-realtime.config.ts → HUNG: jest process alive 3h+ at 0.0% CPU (open ws/Redis handle keeps the process up; killed pids 28752/28726/28725). Pre-existing condition in an untouched spec — the spec last passed 4/4 per phase-00 2026-09-12 entry." and "decide whether the hung integration spec needs a forced-exit fix (its afterAll may leave the publisher's duplicate Redis connection open) — flagging for orchestrator"; the 2026-09-17 13:19 orchestrator entry repeats: "hung realtime-gateway.integration-spec.ts still not rerun (open orchestrator item)". This story closes that open item

Fix the teardown in packages/twenty-server/test/integration/realtime-gateway/realtime-gateway.integration-spec.ts so the process always exits: track every WebSocket opened during tests and close them all in afterAll BEFORE httpServer.close (whose callback never fires while sockets stay open), and close the isolated app's own Redis/pubsub handles that nestApp.close() does not release (the suspected "publisher's duplicate Redis connection")

Prefer real teardown over escape hatches: forceExit in jest-integration-realtime.config.ts is allowed ONLY if a specific open handle is provably outside the test's control, and the reason must be recorded in the report entry — never weaken or delete an existing assertion to reach green (contract rule)
While touching jest-integration-realtime.config.ts, remove the pre-existing unused `const tsConfig` require flagged 2026-09-17 (phase-02-report line 550 warning) — no other config behavior change

Rerun BOTH realtime integration specs to green with clean process exit: NODE_ENV=test npx jest --config jest-integration-realtime.config.ts (gateway spec — 6 tests per current file, last recorded clean run 4/4 on 2026-09-12 — and realtime-publisher-fanout.integration-spec.ts, 2/2 clean since 2026-09-17); the shell prompt must return with exit code 0, no --forceExit where avoidable

Do NOT change any gateway/auth/publisher service source (src/engine/core-modules/realtime-gateway/**) — this is a harness-only story; if the hang reveals a real service defect (a handle genuinely leaked in production code), stop, record it in the report as a flagged defect for a separate slice, and keep the spec green without masking it
Do NOT extend test coverage in this story (that is US-073); do NOT touch the shared jest-integration.config.ts harness or run the 621-spec sweep (Tier 2)
Quality gate: preflight pg_isready -h localhost && redis-cli ping green before the integration run (either failing → report BLOCKED naming the service)
Quality gate: NODE_ENV=test npx jest --config jest-integration-realtime.config.ts green (both spec files) AND the jest process exits cleanly (record elapsed time and exit code)
Quality gate: cd packages/twenty-server && npx tsgo -p tsconfig.json --noEmit exits 0

Quality gate: npx oxlint --type-aware -c .oxlintrc.json <touched files> -> 0 errors / 0 warnings (npx nx lint:diff-with-main twenty-server prints 'No changed files.' on uncommitted slices — direct oxlint is the substitute gate, prior-phase precedent)

Quality gate: dated entry appended to docs/plan/phases/phase-02-report.md recording the repro or non-repro of the hang on HEAD, the exact open handles found (npx jest --detectOpenHandles is acceptable evidence), the fix, and the clean-exit rerun; PLAN.md not edited; nothing committed

userStories.title: P2.1 bullet 5 (Tier-1 portion) — extend the realtime gateway integration spec with subscription-failure acknowledgements and reconnect/seq-cursor semantics
userStories.description: As a platform engineer validating the realtime gateway, I want real-session integration tests covering subscription failure acknowledgements and authoritative reconnect semantics (fresh sequence numbers, no durable replay cursor) so that P2.1 bullet 5's in-process-verifiable acceptance is proven against real sockets and Redis, with the browser/multi-session residual left to the orchestrator.
acceptanceCriteria: PLAN P2.1 bullet 5 (verbatim): "Real-session integration tests for auth, tenant/topic isolation, subscription failure and authoritative reconnect refetch. Per-socket sequence numbers are not durable replay cursors." — this story delivers the integration-spec portion expressible in the existing isolated harness; auth and tenant/topic isolation are ALREADY covered by the 6 existing tests (invalid-token rejection :354, cross-workspace isolation :378, inbox scoping :399) — extend, never rewrite the passing tests

Subscription-failure acknowledgements: subscribing to a topic the authenticated caller is not entitled to (and to a malformed/unknown topic shape) returns a distinct error/nack envelope while the socket stays usable for a later valid subscribe — mirror the established invalid-token pattern in the same spec

Authoritative reconnect semantics: opening a SECOND socket on the same topic after the first closes starts its sequence numbers fresh (no continuation, no replayed backlog) and a fresh subscribe reflects current durable topic state — asserting the PLAN's contract that per-socket sequence numbers are not durable replay cursors

If a case requires DB-backed membership/record state the isolated (Redis + ws, no DB) harness cannot provide — notably record/channel topic ACL revocation journeys (bullet 3's acceptance, which phase-02-report 2026-09-16 entry ties to an installed a2e-chat workspace and the running stack) — do NOT force it: record it in the report entry as the orchestrator residual instead

Tests-only story: no changes to src/engine/core-modules/realtime-gateway/** or any front module; if a new test exposes a real defect, keep the spec honest (do not delete the failing assertion), mark the slice partial/blocked with the exact error, and flag the defect for a separate slice
Keep every existing gateway + fanout integration test green with clean process exit (US-072's teardown must survive the new cases — close the new sockets too)

Do NOT run a browser handshake or multi-instance fan-out proof (Tier 2 — orchestrator; phase-02-report 2026-09-17 13:19 classifies the full bullet 'Tier 2 by nature': this story delivers the contract-Tier-1 integration portion and the report entry must name the residual for orchestrator adjudication)

Quality gate: NODE_ENV=test npx jest --config jest-integration-realtime.config.ts green (both spec files incl. the new cases) AND the jest process exits cleanly
Quality gate: cd packages/twenty-server && npx tsgo -p tsconfig.json --noEmit exits 0
